items.stem: What makes ML CI/CD different from traditional software CI/CD?

options.text: Data and models are versioned and tested, not just code
options.rationale: Correct: ML pipelines must validate data and model quality too.
ML needs more test types, not fewer.

options.text: Code never changes in ML systems
options.rationale: Code still changes and is still tested.

options.text: Deployments are always manual in ML
options.rationale: ML aims to automate deployment like software.

items.explanation: Correct: ML pipelines must validate data and model quality too.

options.rationale: Correct: bad input data must fail the pipeline early.

options.text: A minimum model-performance threshold on a holdout set
options.rationale: Correct: models below the bar should block the merge/deploy.
Linting alone does not catch data or model regressions.
Not a quality signal for ML.

items.stem: Why deploy a new model as a canary first?

options.text: It limits blast radius and lets you compare metrics before full rollout
options.rationale: Correct: canaries expose a small slice so regressions are caught early.

options.text: It guarantees the model is more accurate
options.rationale: Canarying measures impact; it does not improve accuracy.

options.text: It removes the need for monitoring

options.rationale: Canarying is a release strategy, not training.

items.explanation: Correct: canaries expose a small slice so regressions are caught early.
